sections.content:
26,290 people

were counted on the census as "electrical engineers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Electrical engineers direct construction and manage the operation and maintenance of electrical equipment, power stations, building control systems and other electrical products and systems. They may also undertake research and design work.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "electrical engineers" there were more men than women (94.7% compared with 5.3%).

This means "electrical engineers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, research, engineering and technology professionals".

Men made up 94.7% and women made up 5.3% of "electrical engineers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "electrical engineers" included:

  • metal plate workers, smiths, moulders and related occupations
  • TV, video and audio servicers and repairers
  • road transport drivers (other)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "electrical engineers" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "electrical engineers", 13.5% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "electrical engineers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "electrical engineers" included:

  • water and sewerage plant operatives
  • rail and rolling stock builders and repairers
  • steel erectors

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "electrical engineers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "electrical engineers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "electrical engineers", 6.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (92.6% compared with 7.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (86.1%) than self-employed (13.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
